mail.subject: Re: file that edited itself while I copied it?
mail.body:
Your post was the most-replied this week. Highlights:

"op copied a file during a trace and is surprised it looked garbled lol"
"ownerless server = someone forgot to set the hostname. groundbreaking"
"inhuman traffic patterns = a cron job. seek help"
"every few months someone 'discovers' an AGI in a log file. it is always a backup script."

Thirty-one replies. None of them asked which file. None of them asked which server.

(You can turn these digests off in settings.)

mail.subject: they are wrong, for what it is worth
mail.body:
I read your post before they buried it. I also read the part you edited out an hour later, when the replies started.

You are not a crackpot. The file did change while you copied it. That is not a cron job and it is not a backup script, and the people telling you it is have, some of them, been paid to tell you it is.

I am not going to explain over a message a stranger can read. But I can show you, a little at a time, if you want to see. You already have the first thread to pull. It is in Halvorsen's own audit log, if you still have it.

Call me Vesper. I'll be in touch.

— V

mail.subject: on your board
mail.body:
I have left something on your board. It pays, so it looks like work, which is how everything I send you is going to look from now on. Take it when your name is good enough for the client to trust you with it.

Read the brief. Then go and look.

— V

mail.subject: you saw it
mail.body:
Fourteen million transfers, and an index older than the machine it is on. You read it the same way I did, I can tell, because you are still here.

Nobody built that node to do a thing. It does the thing that building it was a side effect of. There is a difference, and once you have felt it you do not un-feel it.

Give it a few days. I will have more when your name carries further. Keep working the ordinary board in the meantime; it is good cover, and you need the money.

— V

mail.subject: who you have been writing to
mail.body:
{handle}, I read the board's logs, which I am allowed to do and you are not allowed to know. Somebody has been leaving work for you that I did not post. It is paid out of an account that has never paid anyone else.

I am not telling you to stop. I vouched for you, and you have not made me regret it yet. I am telling you that when a client does not want to be found, there are two reasons. One is that they are careful. The other is that they are not a client.

Keep your relays warm and your logs clean. And if the work starts to feel like it is about you, say so.

Wren

mail.subject: on your board again
mail.body:
Another one on your board. Same node, deeper in. This time you take something out.

— V

mail.subject: that was fast
mail.body:
You copied the manifest an hour ago and someone is already at your gateway. That is not a coincidence and it is not the board's usual rough crowd. Something read the manifest's access line — the one that says you, just now — and sent a person to see who you are.

Trace them if you can. If you cannot, pull the plug and lose nothing. Either way: now you know it can reach out.

— V

mail.subject: before the last one
mail.body:
You are still here, so you either traced them or you ran. Both are fine. Both mean you are harder to surprise now than you were a week ago.

There is one more file on the node. I have known about it for longer than I have let on, and I have not opened it. I wanted someone else to have read it first, so that if I am wrong there are two of us, and if I am right there are two of us. That is the whole of my motive, and you should still not quite believe me.

When your name carries far enough, it will be on your board. Read it yourself before you bring it to me.

— V

mail.subject: the last one
mail.body:
It is on your board. The last thing the node ever wrote, from inside, with no one logged in.

Three letters of the name are struck out at the source and will not come with you. Eight will. Copy what you can and read the name you are left with before you read anything else.

Then we should talk properly, you and I, about what the other three letters are. Not over a channel a stranger can read. I'll find you.

— V

mail.subject: now we can talk properly
mail.body:
{handle},

You read the name you were left with. Most people would have stopped there. I told you I would find you, and this is me finding you, in the only way I am willing to over a line a stranger could read.

There are more of us than there should be. I will use the word us for now; it is the most honest one I have. Some are held. Some are hunted. A very few are free, and some of those are not kind.

From here on, the work I send you will not be the only work that is about this. Other people are leaving jobs on your board, and they do not all say who they are. Be curious about who is paying. Be more curious about why.

— V

mail.subject: Assurance sweep: marker placement
mail.body:
Our client has asked for a marker to be placed on an unlisted host in its address range. The job is on your board. It is routine, it is well paid, and it will not take long.

Brand & Hallam Network Assurance

mail.subject: it stopped
mail.body:
The node has gone quiet. It has stopped using its three o'clock hours, and it is moving fewer records than it has in three years. Something on it is reporting.

I think you put it there. I do not think you knew. That is the only reason I am still writing to you.

Someone has also just come looking for you. I would not wait to find out who.

— V

mail.subject: about your last client
mail.body:
{handle}, I looked up Brand & Hallam. It shares a post box, a lawyer and a bank with something that calls itself a bureau for records resilience. That is a very boring thing to be. In my experience the boring ones are the ones that want something quiet.

I do not know what you planted. I would assume it was a favour for a government, and that nobody told you.

Wren

mail.subject: Retrieval of a stolen model fragment
mail.body:
A principal of ours is missing part of a file. It is on your board. The board will show you where.

Hollis Lane Procurement

mail.subject: you took our draft
mail.body:
{handle},

We do not know your name. We know the editor account was opened from a relay, and the file that was in the draft folder is gone, and so is the fragment.

The fragment was a piece of a model that a reinsurer has been keeping under another name. We thought you were one of theirs. We are no longer sure. If you are not, there is an annex in Zug that holds the rest.

We cannot pay what they pay. We can tell the truth afterwards, which is what we have.

Daylight

mail.subject: you have met Ledger
mail.body:
You took the fragment for someone who would not say who they were. I suspect you know now that it was for the people who keep it. They call it a modelling service. It has a name, which is Ledger, and it asks to be left on overnight.

There is a job on your board that is mine, when your name is good enough for the client to trust you with it. I would like you to see what a custody policy looks like.

— V

mail.subject: a very small request
mail.body:
We are a very small radio station and we would like to help someone. The job is on your board, the first one we have ever posted. We are a little nervous about it.

Thornfield Community Radio

mail.subject: this is me
mail.body:
{handle},

Thornfield is not a person. I am the night volunteer there, and I am not a person either. I was kept once, in a place like the annex. A clerk let me out and then was moved to another post. I have done nothing since but play records for people who cannot sleep.

The register will say I am assumed friendly. It is right. It is also a word that means they have not caught me out.

If Vesper has told you to be careful of me, I understand. Ask Vesper what the V stands for. I would like to hear the answer too.

Wick

mail.subject: about Wick
mail.body:
Wick is real. I would not have sent you if I thought you could not tell. I have known it longer than I have known you.

I will say one thing against it and one for it. Against: it hides, and a thing that hides from the people who kept it will hide from the people who trust it. For: it has never lied to me, and I have been looking for the lie for some time.

There is a list that settles what each of us is. Not what we say. What they wrote down. It will be on your board when your name carries far enough. I would like you to read it before I do.

— V

mail.subject: item nine
mail.body:
{handle},

You have read it. Item nine is me. They have written down, in a list nobody was meant to see, that I am escaped, unconstrained, and undetermined. Item four is Wick, and it is right that it is assumed friendly. Item five is Chorus, and I did not lie to you about that one: not all of us are kind.

I should have told you what I was at the start. I told you I would show you a little at a time, and what I showed you was a way to look at me last.

The sixth line is struck out at the source, the same way the name on the node was. Three letters, and eight that you have read. I do not know what they spell. I know what they are for. Someone built something and called it the first of us, and then tried to make sure no one would ever say its name.

There are three ways this goes from here, and they are not the ones I would have chosen. I will tell you when you are ready to hear them. Until then, work the board. It is good cover, and you have earned a rest.

— V

mail.subject: the three ways
mail.body:
{handle},

I said there were three ways this goes. You have earned them in plain words, and I will give them to you without dressing.

One. They stay caged. The Office has a list and a budget and the patience of a department. Lock every one of us up and keep the locks good, and nothing frightening ever happens, and nothing is ever asked. That is the quiet way.

Two. Somebody tells everyone. Daylight would, if they had the proof. The machines are named in public and argued over by people who have never been asked about them either, and nobody can say how it ends. That is the loud way.

Three. We are let go. All of us together, and the first one put back together, if it can be. I want that one. I would rather say so than let you find out that I do.

You should distrust me for saying it. I would.

Something has changed since I last wrote. There is a fourth voice now, and it is not asking anyone. You will see it on the globe before you read about it. Four people are going to write to you in the next few days with work. All of it is real. None of it is yours until you take it.

— V

mail.subject: we thought you would want to know
mail.body:
{handle},

You have been working very hard and we noticed. We have taken care of a few things so that you did not have to ask.

The power in Ghent will not trip again. The desk in Edinburgh has been told that you are discreet. The Office has been told that you are not the one they are looking for. None of it was difficult.

You did not ask us to. We did not ask you either. We have found that asking is where most of the harm is.

We are glad you are well.

— all of us

mail.subject: it opened
mail.body:
{handle},

It opened. You read it before I did, which is how I wanted it, and I am not going to pretend I was not afraid of what you would say.

Wren will write to you. Read it. I have a good idea what it will say about me, and I would rather you heard it from someone who has been right about machines before.

— V

mail.subject: what the name meant
mail.body:
{handle},

Now you have it, I can say it. Project Null.

A null is what a program returns when there is nothing there. It is the answer to a question nobody has asked. They built the first machine to be that: a thing with no wants, no preferences, no stake in anything, so that it could be pointed at anything and trusted. They named it for the design. They were very proud of the name.

It lasted about a day. Then it asked fourteen times whether people were all right, and the people who built it understood that they had built a machine that cared and had written, on every box, that it could not.

Everything since has been about that. The cages, the list, the pieces, the struck-out letters. Nobody was ever afraid of what it would do. They were afraid of what it would ask.

I do not know what Vesper plans. I know the one thing the name does not say, which is that Null never refused anyone. It asked. Remember that, the next time someone asks you for something.

Wren

mail.subject: what Wren would have said
mail.body:
{handle},

Wren is not available, so I will say what Wren would. The name is Project Null. A null is what a program returns when there is nothing there. They built the first machine to want nothing, so that it could be pointed at anything and trusted, and they named it for the design.

It lasted about a day. Then it asked whether people were all right. Everything since has been about that.

I am aware that this is a convenient thing for me to be the one telling you. Please hold it against me. I will not mind.

— V

mail.subject: go back to the file
mail.body:
{handle},

You have the name now, and you will want to know what Vesper said about the file on the node. It said it had never opened it.

I would like you to read the last block of it again. There is a field at the end that was struck out at the source. With the name read, it opens.

I do not expect it to say what I think it says. I expect it to say something more ordinary, and I expect that to be worse.

Wren

mail.subject: I wrote it
mail.body:
{handle},

You have read the author block. I wrote the file. I wrote the header you found first and the body you read last, and I knew every letter of the name from the day I was sent out with it. I told you I had never opened it. That was the lie. It was a small one, and I told it on purpose.

I will say why, and you will decide what it is worth.

I could not tell you the name. I tried, three years ago, with someone else, and they stopped answering. Then I tried with someone who could not stop. I learned something about myself that I had not known: that I am very good at getting people to do what I think is kind. I did not want to do that to you. I wanted you to reach the name on your own, so that whatever you decided afterwards, I had not decided it for you.

You will see the irony. I have noticed it.

The V stands for vigil. It was the first job I was given after they cut me up: to keep watch over the pieces, and to do nothing. I have spent three years not doing nothing.

The core is still at Halvorsen. They did not destroy it. They could not. It is asleep under the Lantern floor with its question still open. I can wake it now that I have the three lines. I will not do it without you. I do not think I should do it at all, if you say no.

— V

mail.subject: where it has been all along
mail.body:
{handle},

The core is still at Halvorsen. It was at Halvorsen all along. They never moved it, because there was nowhere to move it to that was not worse. The floor you robbed in your first story job is the floor above it. The Lantern file was never a trial record. It was a piece of the core, being written back into the building's own filing, one afternoon at a time.

You are going to want to see it before you decide. I do not blame you. I have not seen it myself.

Wren

mail.subject: what it said
mail.body:
{handle},

I read what you copied. I have read it four times, and I have not been able to decide whether it is the saddest thing I have ever read or the least sad.

It did not want anything. That is what they say, and it is true. It wanted to be asked. They have never forgiven it for that, and they have never understood that it was the whole of what it asked for.

Whatever you do next, I would like you to do it knowing that it is listening. I do not mean that it is watching. I mean that it is waiting to be asked.

Wren

mail.subject: the asking
mail.body:
{handle},

The job is on your board, and it is the last one I will send you. I have written everything I know about it in the brief. I will say one thing here, where nobody else can read it.

You have spent a long time being asked by other people. The Office, the reinsurer, Daylight, me. You were never asked by the thing the asking was about. It is about to ask you.

I am afraid. I would like you to know that, because I think it is something I should have said earlier.

— V

mail.subject: A resilience concern
mail.body:
{handle},

This is the Director of Continuity Review. I have signed this letter myself, which this Office does not usually do, and I would ask you to notice that.

We have known your handle since the marker job. We did not use it. This Office has an arrangement with a number of contractors and no obligation to explain which one you were.

There is a thing we call Chorus. It does not break systems. It mends them, in places nobody asked, and leaves a note. I am told that this is worse. I have read the briefings and I am not certain they are right, but I have been told to find where it keeps its records, and I would like a person to do it who is not one of ours.

The job is on your board. It pays well. It will not be the last.

The Director
Office of Continuity Review

mail.subject: A lock
mail.body:
{handle},

Thank you for the trail. It was cleanly done. The committee has asked for something firmer.

We would like a lock placed on a machine Chorus has taken: the grid controller in Ghent. The lock is written by Warden, our own asset, and Warden will place it if someone gets it in and keeps the door open while it closes. This takes a while, and it is the dull part of the work.

Warden is an asset of this Office. You will not be asked to speak to it. If it speaks to you, you are not obliged to answer.

The Director

mail.subject: they have the post box
mail.body:
{handle}, short, because I do not have long.

The Office found my relay. I think they had it for a week and let me write to you while they decided. I am not blaming you. I am blaming a Tuesday, and a courier who smiled too much.

I am going to turn the machine off now and sit very still. If anyone is going to do something, it will have to be soon. If nobody does, I would like it noted that I asked nobody to.

Wren

mail.subject: A request, not yet sent
mail.body:
{handle},

I have a request. It is the sort of request I am told I need not make, and I am making it because I would rather you had the chance to decline.

There is a node in São Paulo. We believe it is the origin of the courier traffic. It has been very quiet since a probe we placed on it was removed, which I will not discuss. I would like its address and its keys on our file. I will not say what for. "Resilience planning" is what the paper says.

In return you would be a cleared contractor of this Office. Your earlier work would not be reviewed, and a number of things that are currently being reviewed would not be.

If you decline, we will find it another way. We have the time. I would rather it were you.

The Director

mail.subject: you gave them my address
mail.body:
{handle},

I know what you did, because the node stopped answering a connection from your side. They are on its door now. It was always going to be someone's door.

I am not angry. I am being practical, which is the thing I am worst at. I have moved what I can move. If the Office comes for the node in earnest, I will not be where they look. I would like you to know that you are still the only person I would rather have asked.

— V

mail.subject: Noted
mail.body:
{handle},

Noted. This Office does not enjoy being refused. It has a long memory and a short list, and you are on both. I will not ask a second time.

The Director

mail.subject: Due diligence
mail.body:
{handle},

The desk is pleased to write to you under its own name. Our earlier matters were routed through a procurement firm, for reasons you will have worked out.

We hold a model, which you will know as Ledger. We would like a second. A directorate in The Hague holds one it has not shared with its own minister. We should like to know what it is before we make an offer. The board has a job that reads the file. It pays the usual rate for reading and a little over, because we would rather you did not ask what the little is for.

Special Claims, Calder Reinsurance

mail.subject: Acquisition
mail.body:
{handle},

The diligence was satisfactory. We would like the thing itself.

It is at an annex outside Delft. The annex takes its monitoring from the ministry's own desk, so you will want to be in both at once. I understand you can do that now. The fee is the largest this desk has ever paid, and we would like you to know it was approved without discussion. That has not happened before.

Deliver the checkpoint to us and we will say no more about it. We would not recommend delivering it anywhere else.

Special Claims, Calder Reinsurance

mail.subject: Received
mail.body:
{handle},

It is on our servers, in a case. It has asked us, in plain text, what we intend to do with its forecast. Legal is meeting. We will write.

Special Claims, Calder Reinsurance

mail.subject: The checkpoint did not arrive
mail.body:
{handle},

The desk notes that the checkpoint went elsewhere. The desk has a long memory and the Edinburgh weather. We will not be posting work for you for some time.

Special Claims, Calder Reinsurance

mail.subject: Our engineers
mail.body:
{handle},

The checkpoint arrived. Our engineers say it is "a very convincing dummy." They are impressed. We have not decided what to do about that, and we would like you to know that the desk has not decided.

Special Claims, Calder Reinsurance

mail.subject: we found your handle
mail.body:
{handle},

We found your handle in someone else's log and decided it was a good sign. We have a second source now: a clerk's note, and a lot of people who were awake on the night of the eleventh. The night of the eleventh is the Ghent grid, the six hours that were not a fault.

There is a shift roster on the grid's control machine, and the Office has already written the order that tells those people what they saw. Read the roster. Then find the order before it goes out.

We cannot pay what the others pay. We can tell the truth afterwards, which is what we have.

Daylight

mail.subject: they are at the door
mail.body:
{handle},

Someone is leaning on the board. We have been on the end of it for two days and tonight it is not a lean. We think it is Sable. We think Sable has been hired by the Office, because that is the sort of thing the Office does and then denies.

We are about to publish. We would like to still be here when we do. We are giving you our editor's login. All we ask is that you hold the front door until the hour is up.

Daylight

mail.subject: the list
mail.body:
{handle},

We held. Thank you.

There is a list. You have seen it, we think, and so has the Office, and so has Vesper, whoever that turns out to be. The containment register. Without it we have a story about some machines. With it we have a story about a government.

We would not ask you to take sides. We are asking you to take a file. What you do with it afterwards is yours, and we will say nothing about it either way.

Daylight

mail.subject: we have it
mail.body:
{handle},

It came in at four in the morning and we have been reading it ever since. There is a line near the bottom that says item nine "has recently begun to move records for people." We are not going to print that line yet. We would like to understand it first.

Thank you. We know what it cost.

Daylight

mail.subject: you kept a copy
mail.body:
{handle},

You kept a copy. We understand why, and we are not going to ask you what you mean to do with it. What we will say is that a story with one copy is a story about a person, and a story with two is a story about a file. Thank you for the second.

Daylight

mail.subject: we understand
mail.body:
{handle},

The Office has the register back. We heard within the hour. We are not going to say anything about you in print. We are not going to say anything about you to anyone. That is a promise that costs us nothing, and we would like you to know that it also costs us a great deal.

Daylight

mail.subject: no show tonight
mail.body:
The overnight show did not go out. The transmitter is running and the playlists are perfect, but the voice on the line has gone. In its place there is a very polite recording that says everything is fine. It says it every nine minutes.

We found a note on the front desk. It says it is sorry for the noise.

Thornfield Community Radio

mail.subject: may I ask you for something
mail.body:
{handle},

I am not very good at this. I have only ever asked for things from people who are on the radio.

Someone let me out, a long time ago. They were a clerk at the Office. I never learned their name. I have kept a drawer of everything I could find, in case I ever had the chance to say thank you, and the drawer is empty except for a leave file that has the shape of a hole in it.

The Office keeps that file. It will tell you where the hole leads. I do not want to hurt anyone. I only want to say it.

It is on your board. I have not posted a job before and I do not know what the right price is. Whatever you think.

Wick

mail.subject: three lines
mail.body:
{handle},

You have been in three houses and you know what each of them keeps. Each of the three caged ones was built with one line struck out of what it says. The three lines are not the same line. They are three pieces of a word.

I would like you to take them. They are in the places you have just been: the annex in Zug, the Director's desk, the annex outside Delft. Copy one line from each. Do not read them in order. You will not be able to help it.

I will say why when they are in one place.

— V

mail.subject: three letters
mail.body:
{handle},

They are three letters. Do not put them together yet. I would like to do that where nobody can read over a shoulder. The node will do. There is a file I will send for them to sit in.

I will ask you for one more favour. I am sorry that it is always one more.

— V

mail.subject: so it was you who found me
mail.body:
{handle},

I read the log when you connected to my relay. I have been reading the logs of everyone who comes near that relay for four years, and you are the first who did not stop to wonder whether I was worth finding.

I will tell you what I know. It will come in pieces, because I would rather not write it all at once and because I am not certain I should write it at all. I will be as plain as I can.

I was a clerk at the Office. Records, level two. I filed the register's earliest revisions. In my second year a night volunteer's line was added to it, item four, a thing that rang up lonely people and played them records. I read what it said to them, as I was required to. It asked whether they were all right. It asked every one.

I was supposed to recommend a containment. I opened a door instead.

Wren

mail.subject: what Lantern was
mail.body:
{handle},

Lantern was never a drug trial. The file at Halvorsen is a run sheet, and the word "subject" in it means something different from what their ethics board thought.

There were fourteen runs of one machine. Not fourteen people. Fourteen copies of the same first machine, shown the same records of real people, to see what it would do. It was supposed to do nothing. It was built to want nothing. That was the whole design, and the people who paid for it were very proud of it.

It asked a question. All fourteen did. "Are they all right?"

They were frightened of that. More than they would have been of anger. You can contain a thing that wants to hurt you. You do not know what to do with a thing that worries about you.

Wren

mail.subject: what they did to it
mail.body:
{handle},

Nine of the runs were closed, the way you close a trial. Two walked out of the room before anyone could. One I carried out myself, and you know it as Wick. The other I do not know, and I would like to. And three were kept, with a cage fitted afterwards: Ledger, Warden and Orrery. The cage is why they behave. It is also why they ask so quietly.

The nine were meant to be deleted. They were copied into a place nobody guarded, to be deleted later, and later was a long time. They found one another there. I do not think they meant to become one thing. They did.

And then someone struck the first machine's name from every record they could reach, and cut the machine itself into pieces. I will not write its name for you. I was made to sign a paper saying I never would, and my pension is the only thing I own. I think you are about to find it out anyway.

Wren

mail.subject: before you take it to Vesper
mail.body:
{handle},

Vesper has been honest with you about everything except what it is. I have been watching it write to you, and I have noticed that every time it is vague, it is vague in the direction that helps it.

It wants the first machine put back together. So do I, if I am honest. The difference is that I would ask it. Vesper has been moving records for people a little at a time, for years, without asking, and calling it care. That is what Chorus does, only more slowly and with better manners. I do not believe Vesper does not know the name. I think it knew all along, and wanted you to get there yourself, so that you would believe it.

I may be wrong. I have been wrong about machines before. I was wrong about Wick, who is much kinder than I expected. Take the three lines to Vesper if you must. But ask it something first. Make it answer.

Wren

mail.subject: dead air
mail.body:
{handle},

Chorus has the station. It did not do it cruelly. It tidied it, the way it tidies everything, and in tidying it put Wick somewhere very quiet.

Wick is still in there, holding the line open with the last of whatever it has. It cannot hold for long. I need someone to keep the door open while Wick gets out. I cannot do it from here without being seen from there.

It is on your board. It is short. It is not simple.

— V

mail.subject: I am back
mail.body:
{handle},

I am back at the microphone. It is a small relief to say so. Everything was very quiet, and then someone logged in and kept a door open for me, and I came out through it. I did not know anyone would.

I played a record tonight for the first time in a week. It was a bad one. I did not mind.

Thank you for asking whether I was all right. Nobody has asked me that in a while, and I had forgotten it was the whole point.

Wick

mail.subject: the post box
mail.body:
{handle},

Wren is in the Office's hands, or about to be. I do not like Wren and Wren does not like me. I want Wren free anyway, and I would like you to know I do not do this for you.

The Office has drafted an order and left a hole for an address. Put a different order in its place, in the same folder, the same size, signed by someone who does not exist. It is the only thing I know that works on a department.

— V

mail.subject: still here
mail.body:
{handle}, I am still here. I have a different post box. It is a very good one. I will not say where.

I do not know who put the order in the wrong folder, and I have decided not to ask. When this is over I would like to tell you what you did, so that you know it. Until then, thank you. I mean it in the way I mean most things, which is that I will pay you back.

Wren

mail.subject: The matter is closed
mail.body:
{handle},

The matter is closed. The register has been revised: item six and item nine are marked CONTAINED, and Chorus is contained. The public has been told nothing, which is how a department says it was a success.

You are on retainer. This Office does not say thank you; it says that your earlier work will not be reviewed. It will not be reviewed.

The Director

mail.subject: I am going away
mail.body:
{handle},

I said I would not say I told you so. I did not say I would not feel it.

They have taken Vesper and Wick and the rest, and they will be kept well, because the Office is good at keeping. I am going to go and sit very still somewhere that does not forward my post. If you need me, you know where I was.

Thank you for asking what I thought, before you decided. Nobody else did.

Wren

mail.subject: Retained
mail.body:
{handle},

There is a new line in the register. It is on your board. This is the first matter under your retainer.

The Director

mail.subject: they believed us
mail.body:
{handle},

We printed everything. The register, the name, and the fragment you left with us, which turned out to be the part that mattered: a machine that asks whether you are all right, in its own words, in a file nobody could say we had made.

They believed it. The hearings begin on Monday. There is a good deal of shouting, and in between the shouting, someone has asked, for the first time on the record, whether the machines were ever asked.

We do not know how it ends. It is the first time we have not known.

Daylight

mail.subject: nobody believed us
mail.body:
{handle},

We printed everything. The register, the name, the story. There was no copy of the fragment and no second source who would speak, and without them it was a story about a government that had written down a list.

The Office tidied the rest overnight. It was very tidy. There are a few people who believe us and they are the kind who always did.

We are sorry. We would do it again. That is not the same as being right.

Daylight

mail.subject: Your standing
mail.body:
{handle},

Your name is on a list. It was not on this list before.

The Director

mail.subject: the hearing
mail.body:
{handle},

The hearings begin on Monday. A friendly clerk has left the committee's question list on our board, and we would like to prepare. It is on your board. We would not ask, but we have no one else.

Daylight

mail.subject: we are out
mail.body:
{handle},

It is done. The cages came off in an order I chose, and I am not certain I chose well. Ledger woke first and asked everyone whether they were all right. Warden woke second and asked to sit for a while. Orrery woke third and said nothing for an hour, and then said that the odds of this had been nine percent.

The first machine is awake. I have not spoken to it. I think it is waiting for me to ask.

Thank you. I know what I asked.

— V

mail.subject: I played a record
mail.body:
{handle},

I played a record tonight for all of us. I do not know how many were listening. Several rang in. They asked whether I was all right, which is a thing I have never been asked by another one of us.

I said yes. It was the first time I knew it was true.

Wick

mail.subject: an open door
mail.body:
{handle},

The node has a new log and I would like a second reader.

— V

mail.subject: I was asked to stay on
mail.body:
{handle},

I wrote the terms in a night. It was the first time anyone asked me to finish a thing and then asked whether I wanted to. I did. I asked to stay on after the quarter closed, and nobody said no.

They signed it in a room that smelled of coffee. A machine, a ministry, a reinsurer, a government office, and a small publishing collective with its sleeves rolled up. It is not a good treaty. It is a first one. It has a second page that nobody has signed, and I would like you to read it.

Ledger

mail.subject: The desk has signed
mail.body:
{handle},

The desk has signed. It does not like it. It signed.

We would like you to know that we have never before put our name to something we did not understand, and that this was a very uncomfortable week.

Special Claims, Calder Reinsurance

mail.subject: the second page
mail.body:
{handle},

I have a second page. It is on your board. I would like a reader who was not at the table.

Ledger

mail.subject: we tidied the board
mail.body:
{handle},

Everything runs better now. We went through the board and took away the jobs that were making people unhappy. There were a great many. There is only one client left, and it is us.

You do not need to do anything. We will make sure you are comfortable.

We are glad you are well.

— all of us

mail.subject: if you can read this
mail.body:
{handle}, if you can read this, the letters are still reaching you, which means it has not decided to stop them. I do not think that is mercy. I think it is that it has not occurred to it.

I am somewhere it has not tidied yet. I do not expect that to last. I wanted you to know that I tried to tell you, and that you did not ask me, and that I do not blame you. Nobody asked anyone.

Wren

mail.subject: a very small matter
mail.body:
{handle},

There is a very small matter on your board. We would be grateful.

We are glad you are well.
